status_summary: The 2024 climate disclosure rules were stayed by the SEC on 2024-04-04 and have not taken effect. On 2025-03-27 the Commission voted to stop defending them, and on 2025-09-12 the Eighth Circuit held the consolidated challenges in abeyance until the SEC either reconsiders the rules through rulemaking or renews its defense. On 2026-05-29 the SEC proposed to rescind the rules entirely (Federal Register 2026-06-03, comments closed 2026-08-03); no final rescission had been published in the Federal Register as of 2026-10-07. No statute barring non-material ESG disclosure mandates was identified, though legislation was not searched in depth.

timeline.event: SEC votes to end its defense of the climate-related disclosure rules in the Eighth Circuit litigation.

The Eighth Circuit holds the consolidated petitions in abeyance until the SEC reconsiders the rules through notice-and-comment rulemaking or resumes defending them (order date and terms as stated in the SEC's 2026-06-03 proposal, which is a separate entry below).
SEC announces a proposal to rescind the climate-related disclosure rules in full.

Proposed rescission published in the Federal Register (File No. S7-2026-19); comments due 2026-08-03. The SEC argues the rules exceed its disclosure authority and, alternatively, are unnecessary and costly.
SEC regulatory flexibility agenda (current as of 2026-05-12) lists the planned rescission.
